nodes.name: C15-(IrRh)2PrNdTb Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Metal acetylacetonate precursors with a molar ratio of Ir:Rh:Pr:Nd:Tb = 3:3:1:1:1 were loaded on carbon support (Vulcan XC-72R), mechanically mixed with calcium hydride (CaH₂) and NaCl-KCl eutectic mixture, and annealed at 700°C under 5% H₂/Ar atmosphere for 2 h. During the stage of temperature ramping, Ir and Rh were preferentially reduced and alloyed due to their higher standard reduction potentials than rare earth elements. As the temperature increased to 700°C, Pr/Nd/Tb were reduced by CaH₂ with the assistance of the molten salt medium and then incorporated into IrRh alloy, forming disordered A1-(IrRh)₂PrNdTb. With the annealing duration to 2 h at 700°C, a thermodynamically driven phase transition occurred, reconstructing the disordered A1-(IrRh)₂PrNdTb into ordered C15-(IrRh)₂PrNdTb.
nodes.source_text: High entropy topologically close-packed C15-(IrRh)2PrNdTb nanocrystals were synthesized by a molten-salt assisted reduction approach (Figure 1a). Typically, metal acetylacetonate precursors... annealed at 700°C under 5% H₂/Ar atmosphere for 2 h.

nodes.name: A1-(IrRh)2PrNdTb Synthesis (Control)
nodes.procedure: Metal acetylacetonate precursors with a molar ratio of Ir:Rh:Pr:Nd:Tb = 3:3:1:1:1 were loaded on carbon support (Vulcan XC-72R), mechanically mixed with calcium hydride (CaH₂) and NaCl-KCl eutectic mixture, and annealed at 700°C under 5% H₂/Ar atmosphere for less than 2 h (shortened annealing duration to prevent phase transition).
nodes.source_text: For comparison, control samples of A1-(IrRh)₂PrNdTb... were also synthesized.

nodes.name: C15-Ir2Pr Synthesis (Control)
nodes.procedure: Ir and Pr acetylacetonate precursors were loaded on carbon support (Vulcan XC-72R), mechanically mixed with calcium hydride (CaH₂) and NaCl-KCl eutectic mixture, and annealed at 700°C under 5% H₂/Ar atmosphere for 2 h using similar molten-salt assisted reduction approach.
nodes.source_text: For comparison, control samples of A1-(IrRh)₂PrNdTb and C15-Ir₂Pr were also synthesized.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of C15-(IrRh)2PrNdTb and C15-Ir2Pr match standard diffraction pattern of Ir2Pr (PDF#12-0325), indicating C15 structure with Fd3m space group. A1-(IrRh)2PrNdTb shows FCC Ir pattern (PDF#06-0598) with peaks shifted to higher angles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1b, the X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of both C15-(IrRh)₂PrNdTb and C15-Ir₂Pr match well with the standard diffraction pattern of Ir₂Pr (PDF#12-0325)...

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM reveals C15-(IrRh)2PrNdTb nanocrystals with average diameter ~20 nm, nanoporous morphology with 3-4 nm pores, lattice spacing 0.273 nm for (220) facet, and alternating atomic layers along <001> direction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy images (HAADF-STEM) reveal that the C15-(IrRh)₂PrNdTb nanocrystals are uniformly distributed with an average diameter of approximately 20 nm...

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping confirms uniform distribution of Ir, Rh, Pr, Nd, and Tb atoms within C15-(IrRh)2PrNdTb, A1-(IrRh)2PrNdTb, and C15-Ir2Pr nanocrystals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping confirms the uniform distribution of Ir, Rh, Pr, Nd, and Tb atoms within the C15-(IrRh)₂PrNdTb nanocrystals (Figure 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS shows Ir/Rh/Pr/Nd/Tb atomic ratio in C15-(IrRh)2PrNdTb as 32.0:31.3:13.7:10.5:12.5, aligning with C15 phase stoichiometry.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, the inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) suggests that the Ir/Rh/Pr/Nd/Tb atomic ratio in the C15-(IrRh)₂PrNdTb is 32.0:31.3:13.7:10.5:12.5...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ir predominantly in metallic state; Ir⁰ 4f7/2 binding energy in C15-(IrRh)2PrNdTb (61.11 eV) negatively shifted vs A1-(IrRh)2PrNdTb (61.33 eV), indicating electron transfer from rare earths to Ir.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS spectra of Ir 4f indicates that Ir predominantly exists in a metallic state. Notably, the binding energy of the Ir⁰ 4f7/2 peak in C15-(IrRh)₂PrNdTb (61.11 eV) shows a negative shift compared to that of A1-(IrRh)₂PrNdTb (61.33 eV)...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir L3-edge XANES shows C15-(IrRh)2PrNdTb has reduced white-line intensity vs A1-(IrRh)2PrNdTb, indicating lower average Ir valence state closer to Ir foil.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2c, the white-line peak intensities for both C15-(IrRh)₂PrNdTb and A1-(IrRh)₂PrNdTb are situated between Ir foil and IrO₂, but nearer to Ir foil.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Ir-Pr(Nd/Tb) bond length 2.99 Å and Ir-Ir(Rh) 2.60 Å in C15-(IrRh)2PrNdTb vs 2.82 Å and 2.66 Å in A1-(IrRh)2PrNdTb; higher coordination number in C15 structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EXAFS fitting results reveal that the Ir-Pr(Nd/Tb) bond length in C15-(IrRh)₂PrNdTb (2.99 Å) is longer than that of A1-(IrRh)₂PrNdTb (2.82 Å), while the Ir-Ir(Rh) bond in C15-(IrRh)₂PrNdTb (2.60 Å) is slightly compressed...

nodes.characterization_summary: CV with different scan rates gives double-layer capacitance Cdl = 23.4 mF cm⁻² for C15-(IrRh)2PrNdTb (highest among samples) to evaluate ECSA; also used for H* desorption peak analysis showing negative shift vs references.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the double-layer capacitance (Cdl) was calculated from cyclic voltammetry (CV) curves with different scan rates to evaluate the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) of the studied catalysts... C15-(IrRh)2PrNdTb exhibits the highest Cdl value (23.4 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows C15-(IrRh)2PrNdTb has higher proportion of alkali metal cation hydrated water (AM-H2O) at ~3600 cm⁻¹ than A1-(IrRh)2PrNdTb and C15-Ir2Pr, especially under cathodic polarization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At the open-circuit potential, C15-(IrRh)₂PrNdTb exhibits a significantly higher proportion of AM-H₂O than A1-(IrRh)₂PrNdTb and C15-Ir₂Pr.
